title: Bed and breakfast or small hotel

fields.label: The building
fields.help: What kind of house it is, the brick or stone, the colour of the front door.

fields.label: Rooms and prices
fields.help: Each room with who it sleeps, the bed, size, nightly price and anything special about it.

fields.label: Check-in, breakfast and minimum stays
fields.help: Check-in time, breakfast hours, weekend prices and minimum nights.

fields.label: What's nearby
fields.help: Places guests love, with minutes on foot and roughly which way.

fields.label: Brand colour
fields.help: Optional: your door or logo colour.

writerNotes: house: the brick (red, brown, stone or white) closest to the building, and its front door's colour. The hero shows five guest rooms in the colours of the first five rooms; stay.room is the room the guest is shown up to (pick a favourite, and name it in the third stage).
rooms.list: the brief's rooms exactly (prices, beds, who they sleep), each with a short line and two colours that suit it (soft wall colour, a stronger throw).

key: rooms count, check-in time, breakfast hours and minutes to town, short enough to fit (up to nine characters each). sign: one or two places at the corner with their minutes. stay.clock is 12h in the US, otherwise 24h.
stages: the six steps of a night in this place, in its own voice: arriving at dusk, checking in, your room, lights out, breakfast, out for the day.

dates: what a Friday or Saturday night adds (0 if nothing) and the fewest nights for a weekend stay, from the brief. The request really sends: the request goes to the house, who confirm it. Never say it is booked, paid or confirmed.
nearby: three to six places from the brief with minutes on foot and which way they lie (degrees from north, roughly), and two rings for the map (e.g. 5 and 10 minutes).

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop); section titles have a second half. theme.accent is the house's colour, deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
